source: NPTEL Week 1 assessment, Jul–Oct 2026 run (accepted answers, reworded)

questions.question: Which pair of words would most likely have similar word embeddings?
questions.explanation: Synonyms appear in nearly identical contexts, so their vectors end up closest. (Dog/cat are related but not interchangeable.)

questions.question: Which statement about TF-IDF is FALSE?
options: It measures how important a word is to a document relative to the corpus
TF reflects how often a term appears in a document; IDF reflects how rare it is across documents
A high TF-IDF score means the term is common across all documents and so not very important
It is used for document classification and information retrieval
questions.explanation: The reverse is true: a high score means the word is frequent in this document but rare elsewhere, so it is distinctive. Words common everywhere get a low IDF.

questions.question: Which is the correct order of steps in an NLP pipeline (per the course)?
questions.explanation: Tokenize first; POS tags are needed for accurate lemmatization; NER comes last on the processed tokens.

questions.question: In NLP, a "corpus" is:
options: A large collection of texts used to train a model
Only the labels in supervised learning
A random subset of training words
questions.explanation: Corpus = the body of text the model learns from.

questions.question: In a sentiment-analysis workflow, text is turned into numerical vectors during:
questions.explanation: Vectorisation (BoW, TF-IDF, embeddings) is part of pre-processing, before the classifier runs.

questions.question: Why is data cleaning done in sentiment analysis?
options: To remove noise and irrelevant information
questions.explanation: Cleaning strips HTML, URLs, punctuation noise, stop words, etc.

questions.question: Sub-word tokenization helps a language model by:
options: Splitting rare or unseen words into smaller frequent pieces

questions.question: According to the course, how does a sparse matrix help in generative AI models?
options: It compresses large data, cutting memory use and computation
It removes irrelevant points to raise accuracy
questions.explanation: Storing only non-zero entries saves memory and skips useless computation.

questions.question: "Natural language" in AI means:
options: Any language humans speak, such as English or Hindi
questions.explanation: NLP deals with human languages, as opposed to formal/programming languages.

questions.question: How do language models pick up acronyms, abbreviations and maths expressions during training?
options: By tokenizing them and learning their context from a large corpus
questions.explanation: They are just tokens; meaning comes from the contexts they appear in.
